ilt.explanation: "Ilt" means "oxygen". To say a patient is given oxygen, say: "Patienten får ilt" (The patient is getting oxygen). Do not mix it up with "ild" (fire), which differs by one letter: "Man må ikke lege med ild" (You must not play with fire).

imellem.explanation: "Imellem" means "between". To say something sits in the space of two things, say: "imellem to huse" (between two houses). To say something happens from time to time, use "en gang imellem" (once in a while): "Jeg ser hende en gang imellem" (I see her once in a while).

imens.explanation: "Imens" means "while". It is built from "i" (in) and "mens" (while). To say what happens during the wait, start a second sentence with it, where it means "meanwhile": "Jeg laver mad. Imens dækker du bord" (I am cooking. Meanwhile you set the table).

immunitet.explanation: "En immunitet" means "an immunity". To say someone cannot catch an illness, add "mod" (against): "Hun har immunitet mod influenza" (She has immunity to the flu). In law, the word means protection from prosecution: "diplomatisk immunitet" (diplomatic immunity).

imod.explanation: "Imod" means "against". To say you play against someone, say: "Vi spiller imod dem" (We play against them). To say you move toward something, it means "toward": "Hun gik imod døren" (She walked toward the door).

imponerende.explanation: "Imponerende" means "impressive". It comes from the verb "at imponere" (to impress). To talk about the person who feels it, use "imponeret" (impressed): "Jeg er imponeret" (I am impressed).

imponeret.explanation: "Imponeret" means "impressed". It comes from the verb "at imponere" (to impress). To say what impressed you, add "over" (about): "Jeg er meget imponeret over resultatet" (I am very impressed with the result). Do not mix it up with "imponerende" (impressive), which describes the thing that impresses: "et imponerende resultat" (an impressive result).

import.explanation: "En import" means "an import". It is the noun for the verb "at importere" (to import). To talk about goods leaving the country, use the opposite, "en eksport" (an export): "Firmaet lever af eksport" (The company lives off export).

impulsiv.explanation: "Impulsiv" means "impulsive". It comes from the noun "en impuls" (an impulse). To say you bought something without planning, say: "Det var et impulskøb" (It was an impulse buy).

ind.explanation: "Ind" means "in". To tell someone to come into a room, say: "Kom ind!" (Come in!) To say the place you enter, add "i" (in) after it: "Hun løber ind i butikken" (She runs into the store). To say someone is already inside, use "inde" (inside): "Han er inde" (He is inside).

indadvendt.explanation: "Indadvendt" means "introverted". It is built from "indad" (inward) and "vendt" (turned), so it means "turned inward". To describe someone who likes meeting people, use the opposite, "udadvendt" (outgoing): "Hun er meget udadvendt" (She is very outgoing).

indbydende.explanation: "Indbydende" means "inviting". It comes from the verb "at indbyde" (to invite). To say something looks tempting, say: "Vandet så indbydende ud" (The water looked inviting).

indefra.explanation: "Indefra" means "from the inside". To say where a lock is, say: "Døren er låst indefra" (The door is locked from the inside). To say from the outside, use the opposite, "udefra": "Døren kan kun åbnes udefra" (The door can only be opened from the outside).

inden.explanation: "Inden" means "before". To say something happens before a time, put the time after it: "Vi er hjemme inden middag" (We are home before dinner). Do not mix it up with "indenfor" (inside), which is about a place: "Vi er indenfor" (We are inside).

indenfor.explanation: "Indenfor" means "inside". To invite someone in from the door, say: "Kom indenfor!" (Come in!) To say within a time, say: "indenfor en uge" (within a week).

indeni.explanation: "Indeni" means "inside". To say what the inside of a thing is like, say: "Æblet er råddent indeni" (The apple is rotten inside). To talk about feelings you hide, say: "Hun smiler, men hun er ked af det indeni" (She smiles, but she is sad inside).

indenlandsk.explanation: "Indenlandsk" means "domestic". It is built from "inden" (within) and "land" (country). To talk about goods from another country, use the opposite, "udenlandsk" (foreign): "udenlandske varer" (foreign goods).

inderst.explanation: "Inderst" means "at the very back". It is the "most" form of "indre" (inner). To talk about true feelings, use "inderst inde" (deep down): "Inderst inde er han bange" (Deep down he is afraid).

indflydelsesrig.explanation: "Indflydelsesrig" means "influential". It is built from "indflydelse" (influence) and "rig" (rich), so it means "rich in influence". To say who is affected, add "på" (on) after "indflydelse": "Han har stor indflydelse på sine kolleger" (He has great influence on his colleagues).

indfødsret.explanation: "En indfødsret" means "a citizenship". It is built from "indfødt" (native) and "ret" (right). In Denmark, a new citizen is granted "indfødsret" by a law passed in parliament.

indfødt.explanation: "Indfødt" means "native", as in born in a place: "en indfødt københavner" (a native Copenhagener). It is built from "ind" (in) and "født" (born).

indhold.explanation: "Indholdet" means "the content". It comes from the verb "at indeholde" (to contain). The list at the front of a book is "en indholdsfortegnelse" (a table of contents).

indien.explanation: "Indien" means "India". To say a person is from India, use "en inder" (an Indian person): "Han er inder" (He is an Indian). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Hun er indianer" (She is a Native American).

indimellem.explanation: "Indimellem" means "now and then". It is built from "ind" (in) and "imellem" (between). To say someone does something from time to time, say: "Hun ringer indimellem" (She calls now and then).

indisk.explanation: "Indisk" means "Indian", from "Indien" (India). To talk about a person from India, use "en inder" (an Indian person). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Han er indianer" (He is a Native American).
